The expansion lets traders track and trade equities and commodities issued on-chain, including assets from xStocks and Ondo. The […]
content: Guardis, an on-chain trading and security platform based in Costa Rica, has announced the addition of tokenized stocks and commodities to its services. This expansion enables traders to track and trade on-chain issued equities and commodities, featuring assets from providers such as xStocks and Ondo, enhancing its overall trading and security capabilities.
content_ta: Costa Rica-வை தளமாகக் கொண்ட ஆன்-செயின் வர்த்தகம் மற்றும் பாதுகாப்பு தளமான Guardis, தனது சேவைகளில் டோக்கன் செய்யப்பட்ட பங்குகள் மற்றும் பொருட்களின் (commodities) சேர்த்தலை அறிவித்துள்ளது. இந்த விரிவாக்கம், xStocks மற்றும் Ondo போன்ற வழங்குநர்களின் சொத்துக்கள் உட்பட, ஆன்-செயினில் வெளியிடப்பட்ட பங்குகளையும் பொருட்களையும் வர்த்தகம் செய்ய வர்த்தகர்களுக்கு உதவுகிறது.

title: Crypto vs Stocks: What the 200-Day Moving Average Shows Now
summary: BTC and ETH are among 88 top-100 cryptocurrencies above their 200-day MA, while most of those coins also hold above shorter-term trends.
content: A recent analysis comparing cryptocurrencies to traditional stocks using the 200-day moving average reveals strong performance in the digital asset market. Major assets like BTC and ETH are among dozens of top-100 cryptocurrencies currently trading above this key long-term indicator. Furthermore, most of these coins are maintaining their positions above shorter-term market trends, signaling resilient momentum across the sector.
content_ta: கிரிப்டோகரன்சிகள் மற்றும் பாரம்பரிய பங்குகளின் நிலையை 200-நாள் மூவிங் ஆவரேஜ் மூலம் ஒப்பிட்டுள்ள சமீபத்திய பகுப்பாய்வு, டிஜிட்டல் சொத்து சந்தையின் வலுவான செயல்திறனைக் காட்டுகிறது. BTC மற்றும் ETH போன்ற முக்கிய சொத்துக்கள், இந்த முக்கிய நீண்ட கால காட்டிக்கு மேல் வர்த்தகமாகும் டாப்-100 கிரிப்டோகரன்சிகளில் அடங்கும். மேலும், இந்த நாணயங்களில் பெரும்பாலானவை குறுகிய கால சந்தை போக்குகளுக்கும் மேல் தங்கள் நிலைகளைத் தக்கவைத்துக்கொள்கின்றன.

title: Mint launches its Web3 gaming platform with focus on player progression
summary: Player experience and progression are at the heart of Mint's latest update.
content: Mint has officially launched its new Web3 gaming platform, placing a strong emphasis on player experience and progression. The latest update is designed to keep players engaged by focusing closely on how they advance through the gaming ecosystem. This move highlights Mint's ongoing commitment to enhancing decentralized gaming and offering more immersive, rewarding journeys for users.
content_ta: Mint தனது புதிய Web3 கிமிங் தளத்தை அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக அறிமுகப்படுத்தியுள்ளது. இது வீரர்களின் அனுபவத்திற்கும் முன்னேற்றத்திற்கும் முக்கியத்துவம் அளிக்கிறது. கிமிங் சுற்றுச்சூழல் அமைப்பில் வீரர்கள் எவ்வாறு முன்னேறுகிறார்கள் என்பதில் கவனம் செலுத்தி, அவர்களை ஈடுபாட்டுடன் வைத்திருக்க இந்த புதிய அப்டேட் வடிவமைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது. பரவலாக்கப்பட்ட கிமிங்கை மேம்படுத்துவதிலும், பயனர்களுக்கு மிகவும் ஈர்க்கக்கூடிய பயணங்களை வழங்குவதிலும் Mint-இன் தொடர்ச்சியான அர்ப்பணிப்பை இந்த நடவடிக்கை எடுத்துக்காட்டுகிறது.

title: Mysterious Spike on XRP Ledger: 400% Rise in New Accounts
summary: XRP Ledger account creation surged more than fourfold above its 30-day average, signaling an unusual burst of network activity.
content: The XRP Ledger recently experienced a significant spike in network activity, with the creation of new accounts surging by over four hundred percent compared to its thirty-day average. title: Ripjar ramps up AI in customer screening to disrupt global economy of crime
summary:
Ripjar, the provider of smarter screening and risk intelligence solutions, has introduced new AI innovations within ULTRA, the real intelligence engine that powers screening operations at financial institutions and enterprises, including 25% of the Global Systemically Important Banks and 35+ of the Global Fortune 500. The updates enable compliance teams to identify and manage risk with greater confidence, speed and clarity, making screening more intelligent, explainable and actionable at scale. 
Built on national security grade technology, ULTRA delivers a level of accuracy and efficiency that off-the-shelf tools and generic LLMs simply cannot match. Powered by proprietary graph algorithms, transformer models and custom AI, the engine resolves more than 10 billion historic articles and over 5 million new articles a day, across more than 150 languages, into a single system of record for entity risk. 
By blending multiple data sources, including PEPs, sanctions, watchlists and adverse media, into one resolved profile, users gain a complete 3D view of risk. Risk lands on the right entity, with 98.7% accuracy, reducing the volume of alerts reaching an analyst by 99%. The engine continues to learn, so an analyst resolves an entity once and gets the benefit for the lifetime of that customer relationship. 
The latest innovations include enhancements to Screening Assistant, Ripjar’s agentic AI capability for alert triage, to further reduce routine alert handling, improve decision-making and increase risk coverage. Updates to ULTRA’s entity matching means customers can now better distinguish between parent organisations, subsidiaries and similarly named group entities. This removes guesswork and strengthens Screening Assistant’s ability to mimic human reasoning when deciding whether or not an alert relates to the exact entity. The update also extends Screening Assistant's handling of complex naming conventions, including Arabic names, to support more global use cases.
Ripjar has also enhanced ULTRA’s adverse media risk classifiers, which analyse each news article to determine if it relates to a specific risk and identify the person involved. The latest model upgrades ULTRA to a new generation of machine learning, improving the quality of existing classification and entity-resolution tasks.
ULTRA is proven in highly regulated and mission-critical environments where explainability and governance are vital. Every alert, decision and summary is backed by evidence, traceable to its source and held in an auditable system of record built for regulatory scrutiny.
Conrad Nicholas, Chief Product Officer at Ripjar, said: "ULTRA is one engine, but it runs multiple layers of AI, each performing a specific task: stripping out duplicate noise, resolving mentions across billions of articles into single entity profiles, and attributing risk to the right person. It works like a funnel, with each layer building on the last. What sets ULTRA apart is orchestrating these models at scale with explainability built in, so customers can trust the outcomes as well as benefit from more efficient screening.” 
Matt Mills, CEO at Ripjar, said: "Knowing who you’re doing business with is becoming more difficult. Sanctions change rapidly, adverse media multiplies and AI is enabling criminals to become more sophisticated. AI is vital but compliance teams need to understand and trust its decision making. We understand the importance of this in part due to our background in the UK’s intelligence services. ULTRA is the result of years of engineering and proven deployments and these latest innovations take explainability and performance to new levels.”

The updates feature advanced agentic AI, improved entity matching for complex naming conventions, and upgraded adverse media risk classifiers. These enhancements aim to help compliance teams identify financial crime risks with greater speed, accuracy, and regulatory explainability at scale.

title: New Monzo Business Money Moves Report Reveals UK SMEs Are Gearing Up for Growth Despite Economic Headwinds
summary:
Monzo Business, the digital bank serving over one million business customers, today publishes its first Money Moves Report, taking a pulse check on the SMEs at the heart of the UK economy. Despite rising costs and economic uncertainty, businesses are feeling positive about the year ahead, with more than half (56%) of SMEs confident about their growth prospects over the next year.
Nearly two-thirds (62%) plan or hope to grow their teams over the coming year. But challenges remain: almost half (46%) naming rising costs as one of their biggest barriers to growth over the next year, followed by economic uncertainty (33%) and the tax burden (26%).
Monzo Business customer data also shows shifts in business spending, with bills up 12% over the past year while transport has remained flat.
The 53-minute a day admin burden  
It’s not just the economic environment that can get in the way of growth. Monzo’s research shows that the day-to-day complexity of running a business is creating another significant barrier to growth. UK SMEs currently spend an average of 53 minutes every working day on financial administration, including tasks such as processing invoices and expenses.
Nearly half of businesses (49%) say financial admin takes too long, with 39% saying it actively holds their business back from growing. For some, that means missing opportunities to invest in tech, equipment or premises (21%), pursuing new markets (20%), and hiring staff (18%).
Cutting admin could unlock the next wave of SME growth
Nearly two-thirds (63%) say simpler financial admin would free up time to focus on the things that matter most to their business, such as strategy, sales and building customer relationships. With extra time, one in three (33%) would pursue new customers or markets, 31% would invest in equipment, technology or premises and 26% would hire new staff.
Small businesses want more from their financial tools
Monzo Business customer data also shows spending on software has increased 15% over the last year. Yet, despite businesses putting more money towards technology, more than a third (37%) of SMEs say they are spending more time on financial admin than they were a year ago.
Just 24% agree that their bank actively helps them run their business rather than simply holding their money, as more than half (55%) say they often have to use other tools because their bank doesn’t offer everything they need to manage their finances. This points to growing demand for banking that makes running a business simpler. 
Jordan Shwide, General Manager at Monzo Business, said: “Small businesses are confident about the year ahead and thinking about how they can grow. However, running a business still comes with far too much financial admin, and our research shows that this isn’t simply an inconvenience - it can take time away from growth. 
“At Monzo Business, we want to be a partner in that growth, making business banking simpler and giving owners the tools to spend less time on admin and more time building their business.”
Monzo Business supports 1 in 6 UK businesses with tools designed to make managing finances simpler, from expense cards and tax pots to invoicing and payment links, which help businesses get paid 11 days faster. Read the full Monzo Business Money Moves Report at https://monzo.com/blog to explore the findings.

title: Banks Risk Losing $230 Billion in Payments Revenue as Stablecoins and Tokenized Deposits Go Mainstream
summary:
The global payments industry is approaching a tipping point. As stablecoins, tokenized deposits, and central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) move from experimentation to commercialization, banks face mounting pressure on traditional payments revenue pools. According to the Capgemini Research Institute’s World Payments Report 2027, these instruments are projected to account for approximately 4% of the global payments volume by 2030, impacting high-margin revenue streams such as foreign exchange spreads, correspondent banking, float income, and transaction processing fees.
Banks have prioritized payment innovation for corporate clients over the last three years with 60% identifying it as a strategic area of investment. However, only one in three corporate clients are satisfied with their primary banking partner, revealing a widening gap between what banks are delivering and what businesses increasingly expect.
Nearly three-quarters (74%) of corporates describe cross-border payments as slow, costly, and unpredictable. The end-to-the-end journey for corporate payments, from origination and transfer to confirmation and reconciliation, takes roughly 3.5 days. During that process, more than half (57%) report lacking access to live payment status, cash positions, or transparent pricing. Corporates rank predictability of settlement outcomes, real-time visibility into payment execution, and stronger protection against fraud among their most persistent unmet needs. As a result, corporates incur total costs equivalent to 2% of transaction value for a typical cross-border business-to-business (B2B) payment.
Now in its 22nd edition, the new report surveyed over 1,100 large corporates with revenues greater than USD 1 billion. On average, respondents indicate they operate in 14 markets, maintain 11 banking relationships, and conduct 34% of their B2B payment volume through cross-border transactions. Despite improvements in payment infrastructure, operational fragmentation remains the most defining challenge for corporate clients.
Accelerated intelligent money instruments emerge as a catalyst for transformation
Structural limitations in B2B payment infrastructure, regulatory clarity, and shifting market dynamics are driving the emergence of what the report defines as “accelerated intelligent money” – stablecoins, tokenized deposits, and CBDCs that enable money to do more than simply move between accounts. By supporting 24/7 execution, built-in rules and real-time settlement, these instruments can reduce friction during cross-border payment flows. The report estimates that widespread adoption could unlock as much as USD 4 trillion currently trapped in settlement and liquidity accounts – capital that generates little return and cannot be deployed for lending, investment or other productive uses.
Corporate demand is already building for this new generation of payment instruments and banks remain the preferred provider: 71% of corporates would choose a bank over a fintech for tokenized payments at equivalent cost and quality. However, that preference is not guaranteed. Nearly 60% of corporate clients are willing to source stablecoin services from non-bank providers if their banking partners fail to keep pace. This competitive erosion arrives as corporate clients report 36% of their B2B payment volume already flows through non-banks.
“The payments industry is entering its most significant period of disruption since the emergence of digital banking,” said Jeroen Hölscher, Global Head of Payment Services at Capgemini. “We are moving past the intelligent money hype cycle into a period where the economics and transaction volumes make it impossible for banks to remain on the sidelines. With $230 billion at stake, banks must decide what role they want to play in this emerging ecosystem. A select group of banks have already made their choice and are now shaping the standards and governance that will define the market. Those that act now will build lasting trust, capture new payment flows, and retain the corporate deposits that underpin their wider banking relationships.”
Banks identify tokenized deposits as key priority
As intelligent money moves toward commercialization, banks must define their strategic position in this ecosystem. The report finds that bank executives identify tokenized deposits as the top near-term priority for their ability to remain on balance sheets and fit within existing regulations. However, only 21% of banks – classified as leaders – are actively scaling at least one accelerated intelligent money instrument, while the remaining 79% of banks are still evaluating their position.
These high-achieving banks are focused on specific corporate use cases that address operational friction and monetize their value beyond transaction fees. The payoff is measurable as these leaders are three times more likely than mainstream banks to identify new revenue streams and expect to offset declining transaction revenue within 15 months, versus 25 months for rest of the industry. They are also more decisive: 33% of leaders aim to pursue a transformative market posture by shaping how the ecosystem operates, compared with 40% of mainstream banks that intend to take a reactive approach.
According to the report, since settlement with intelligent money is irrevocable, leaders place a premium on compliance by embedding it directly into execution before money moves. They outpace mainstream banks by 1.5 times on cross-network transaction monitoring and are 1.2 times more likely to both invest in AI-driven surveillance to flag unusual wallet behavior and implement real-time Anti-Money Laundering (AML) and Know Your Customer (KYC) checks into transaction flows.
Yet even among leaders, foundational gaps remain. Just over half (56%) report having the talent and skills to build and maintain digital assets, technical readiness, and capabilities required to support tokenization, smart contracts, and interoperability across financial networks. Closing that gap will determine which banks are best positioned to move from experimentation to scale.

title: Midnite Partners with BR-DGE to Sharpen Payments Performance and Power International Expansion

Pairing Midnite’s product-led, mobile-first platform with BR-DGE’s sector expertise gives their payments team a partner that understands the operational and regulatory realities of gaming at every stage of a transaction.
Before working with BR-DGE, Midnite operated via direct integrations with payment providers in the UK and Ireland. That setup served the business well while it was establishing itself, but rapid growth and ambitious expansion plans meant payments needed to keep pace with the speed and simplicity Midnite already delivers everywhere else in its app. 
As a trailblazer in the industry, Midnite took the same innovative approach to its payment strategy as it has to every other aspect of its business, matching its scaling journey and its customers’ expectations.
Moving to BR-DGE addressed that directly. Jacob Spencer, Chief Revenue Officer at BR-DGE, said: “Midnite built a strong platform on a single PSP, which worked well domestically but limited how quickly they could add new payment methods or move into new markets. Moving to an independent orchestration layer mitigates that technical debt in one step, giving Midnite the scalability they need to match their success and ambitions.
“BR-DGE’s track record and data intelligence capabilities will augment and enrich our orchestration capabilities, enabling Midnite to direct every transaction to achieve optimal performance, even as their business evolves and grows.”
Christian Huynh, Lead Product Manager, Midnite said: “At Midnite, we want every part of the experience to feel built different, and payments are no exception. We’re focused on creating payment experiences that delight our customers, while building the flexibility to innovate quickly and bring the same great experience to new markets as we grow.”

title: Teya Partners with ClearBank to Launch High-Yield Savings Account for Local Businesses
summary:
Teya, the financial services provider supporting local businesses across Europe, today launches Savings Pots, a new savings account with interest paid daily built into the Teya Business Account and powered by ClearBank, the enabler of real-time clearing and embedded banking. 
Now available to existing Teya Business Account holders in the UK, Savings Pots allows business-owners to open pots earning 3% AER (variable) with interest calculated and paid daily. Money in a pot remains instantly accessible, so business-owners can move funds in or out at any time without losing flexibility or facing withdrawal delays.
Teya’s Savings Pots feature has been designed specifically to meet the day-to-day needs of local businesses. It gives them the freedom to set money aside, whether for tax bills, growth plans or a rainy day, all while earning interest, directly within the app they already use.

With Savings Pots, the money a business earns through Teya moves seamlessly from payments into savings, earns interest that is accrued and paid every day and remains instantly accessible when needed, all within Teya, with no separate savings relationship to manage or reconcile.”
Emma Hagan, CEO of ClearBank UK, said: “Teya is an ambitious and innovative business that is moving quickly to give local businesses better ways to manage their money. Carl Hirschson, Senior Product Manager at Teya, said: "Integration speed comes down to the quality of what you're building on. We looked at several ways of doing this and went with ClearBank because their banking infrastructure layer is something we can rely on and build on top of. That's why Savings Pots and our upcoming premium savings product were both built in four months rather than a year. Two products built on one integration."

title: Silverflow and Hypergate Launch Integrated Payment Solution to Accelerate Acquiring Innovation

Hypergate provides PCI DSS Level 1 compliance under its licence alongside DORA-ready documentation, platform stability backed by strict uptime SLAs and robust risk tools, while its configurable routing, cascading and expert orchestration capabilities help payment providers optimise transaction performance. 
The collaboration reflects growing demand across the payments industry for cloud-native infrastructure that enables businesses to replace rigid legacy systems with modern, API-driven platforms capable of supporting faster innovation and greater operational resilience. 

Robert Kraal, Co-founder of Silverflow, said: "The payments industry has reached a point where organisations can no longer afford to be slowed down by fragmented infrastructure and complex integrations. Every additional manual process adds time, cost and operational risk. 
By combining Silverflow's cloud-native processing platform with Hypergate's gateway capabilities, we're giving payment providers a simpler, faster way to launch and scale. Instead of stitching together multiple technologies, customers benefit from an integrated cloud-native ecosystem that reduces complexity while giving them the flexibility and performance modern payments demand." 
Mikhail Goryachkin, COO, said: "Our goal has always been to remove the technical barriers that slow payment businesses down. Working closely with Silverflow allows us to offer customers an integrated solution that combines rapid deployment with enterprise-grade security, compliance and operational flexibility. Together, we're helping payment providers spend less time managing infrastructure and more time growing their business." 
The joint solution is available immediately for organisations looking to modernise their payment infrastructure through an API-first, cloud-native architecture.  
Several modern financial institutions and e-money providers - including Guru Pay, Fairmay, Finsei, and Exepay - are already leveraging the joint solution to power their acquiring ecosystems, combining card processing with wider financial services. 
For these companies, a flexible and scalable gateway is essential. Highlighting this, a representative from Finsei noted: “For us, choosing a gateway was never about adding another technology vendor. It was about strengthening our acquiring proposition. Hypergate gives us the control and agility to improve payment performance while keeping the underlying infrastructure efficient.” This is echoed by Exepay and Fairmay, who value Hypergate's unified API for straightforward merchant onboarding and its pragmatic, hands-on support."
On the processing side, these institutions rely on Silverflow’s modern architecture for greater operational control. A spokesperson from Guru Pay stated that Silverflow provides "interesting reconciliation solutions for IPS reconciliation, a built-in dashboard for dispute management, and clear, comprehensive pricing."
They added: "These features are valuable because acquiring is not only about processing transactions. It is also about having the right visibility, controls, and operational tools behind the scenes."
Exepay also praised the platform's cloud-native infrastructure and direct network connectivity as essential tools for data-driven acquirers.

title: Uniswap v4 Ecosystem Passes 500 Registered Custom Hooks
summary: TL;DR Uniswap’s v4 developer ecosystem has passed 500 registered custom hook deployments in the reported directory data. Hooks let developers customize pool behavior, including fees, liquidity logic and other execution rules. A registered hook is not the same thing as an audited, liquid mainnet market. Uniswap v4’s most important experiment is starting to show scale: developers are increasingly using hooks to customize how liquidity pools behave. The ecosystem has now passed 500 registered custom hook deployments in the reported developer directory data. Hooks Turn Pools Into Programmable Building Blocks Earlier versions of automated market makers were comparatively rigid. A pool followed the protocol’s built-in rules and developers had limited room to change how trading, fees or liquidity management worked. Uniswap v4 hooks change that. They allow developers to run custom logic at specific points in a pool’s lifecycle, opening the door to dynamic fees, specialized liquidity strategies, access controls and more experimental market structures. Passing 500 registered hooks suggests that developers are actively testing that design space rather than treating hooks as a theoretical feature. Registration Does Not Mean Production Readiness The number needs an important caveat. A hook appearing in a developer directory does not mean it has been audited, attracted meaningful liquidity or become a successful mainnet product. Some will remain experiments. Others may never move beyond test deployments. That is normal at this stage. The more useful signal is developer interest. Uniswap v4 is trying to make the AMM itself more modular, allowing teams to build specialized markets without creating an entirely new exchange protocol from scratch. If that model works, the long-term impact could be less about the number of hooks and more about how many new market designs become possible because of them. For now, 500 registrations is a development milestone — not 500 mature DeFi businesses — but it shows the v4 ecosystem is becoming increasingly active. The next stage will be quality rather than quantity. A handful of well-designed hooks that attract deep liquidity could matter more to Uniswap than thousands of experiments that never reach meaningful usage. Auditing will also become a bigger issue because hooks deliberately let developers change pool behavior, increasing the number of assumptions users need to understand. That flexibility is the point of v4, but it also shifts more responsibility toward application developers. The 500-deployment mark therefore shows momentum; the lasting test will be which hook designs become trusted enough to support real capital at scale. This article was written by the News Desk and edited by Samuel Rae.
content: The Uniswap v4 ecosystem has reached a milestone by passing 500 registered custom hook deployments in its developer directory. These hooks enable developers to customize pool behavior such as fees and liquidity logic. However, experts note that registration does not guarantee production readiness, audits, or mainnet liquidity, marking the milestone as an initial indicator of developer interest rather than mature market adoption.

Crux Analytics, the fintech fixing the relationship between financial services companies and the small businesses they serve, has raised $2.2 million in seed funding to help institutions engage, acquire and retain high-potential business relationships, bringing its total funding to $3.2 million.
Crux’s seed round is backed by the very institutions it was built to serve. Castle Creek Launchpad, a joint venture fund with 34 community banks as limited partners, led the raise, with additional participation from Chartway Ventures, One Washington Financial and Curql, three leading credit union investment funds. This funding will enable Crux Analytics to expand its team and accelerate product development as the company capitalises on strong market momentum and a growing portfolio and pipeline of financial services providers, which started with community banks and credit unions and has now expanded organically.
Crux Analytics was founded in 2023 by brothers Jacob and Nathan Bennett, driven by Jacob's firsthand experience of the challenges small businesses face when seeking banking support. As a former small business owner and consultant to Fortune 500 companies, Jacob witnessed how traditional financial institutions consistently underserved small businesses in comparison to their larger counterparts.
Addressing the Challenge of Supporting Small Businesses
Small businesses drive nearly half of all private-sector employment and more than 44% of the U.S.' GDP, yet the key partners supporting them face a fundamental scaling challenge. Serving small businesses is relationship-driven, which requires significant human capital and resources. Large banks can simply hire more people to manage those relationships, but smaller financial services companies need a smarter approach: technology that multiplies their employees' productivity and lets them deliver the trusted-advisor relationship their clients want without exponentially growing their team.
Institutional employees currently spend the majority of their time on the operational tasks required to build a client deal, not on core relationship building with the business owner. Crux replaces the traditional sales enablement stack with a sales execution engine, allowing employees to spend more time closing deals and serving as a trusted advisor.
Community financial institutions remain in robust financial health, operating in a markedly friendlier regulatory environment than they have in years. Community banks closed out 2025 with full-year net income of $29.9B, a 22.5% increase over 2024, with net interest margin reaching 3.77% in the fourth quarter, the highest level since 2018. That strength has carried into 2026: community bank pretax return on assets stood at 1.42% in the first quarter, up 26 basis points year-over-year, and net interest margin remains 24 basis points above its year-ago level.
Credit unions are in equally strong shape: the sector's net worth ratio reached 11.24% in the first quarter of 2026, up from 10.95% a year earlier and more than 60% above the 7% regulatory threshold for a well-capitalized institution, with net income totaling $20.4B at an annual rate, up 30.5% from the same period in 2025.
The platform delivers agentic business development workflows, helping users identify, research and prioritize high-potential prospects, execute targeted personalized outreach, and actively monitor relationships as they evolve. The result is a streamlined workflow that drives new revenue and asset growth, and improves efficiency. Institutions win more small business clients, deepen existing relationships, and build a stickier, more durable client base in the process.
Jacob Bennett, CEO and Co-founder of Crux Analytics, comments: “This funding comes at a critical time. We built Crux for community banks and credit unions, and what we learned there is that the same relationship problem exists across the small business economy. Alternative lenders, commercial insurers and real estate operators all win on relationships, and they all lose time to the operational work that sits behind them. We're giving those teams the infrastructure to act on what they know about their clients, so growth comes from deeper relationships rather than bigger headcount."
Jurgen van de Vyver from Castle Creek Launchpad, said: "Having worked closely with community banks through our strategic limited partners, we've seen how these institutions are built for relationships but lack the operational tools to deliver on that promise at scale. Driving outbound sales has always been a challenge for community banks, which historically have relied on referrals from their local networks. More banks are now looking for new ways to chase organic growth, and their business relationships are crucial to achieving that. Crux Analytics unlocks that potential by automating the manual work so community banks can focus on what matters most, building meaningful relationships with local business owners."
Rob Keatts from Chartway Ventures, added: "The credit union industry has always been built on community relationships, but scaling that approach to serve local businesses has proven difficult. Crux Analytics removes the operational barriers, empowering credit unions to become the community business banking partners they ought to be. When credit unions can proactively support their business members, entire communities benefit from stronger local economies."

title: Solaris goes live on ACI Worldwide platform for Sepa instant payments
summary:
ACI Worldwide, an original innovator in global payments technology, today announced that Solaris, Europe’s leading embedded finance platform, has gone live on schedule on ACI Connetic, ACI’s unified cloud-native platform for intelligent payments orchestration.
The milestone marks the successful completion of the first phase of Solaris' payments modernization initiative. By consolidating its SEPA Instant payments infrastructure onto ACI Connetic, Solaris has strengthened its ability to scale, innovate and adapt in a rapidly evolving payments landscape.
It paves the way for the continued modernization of Solaris' payments infrastructure, as Solaris expands its adoption of ACI Connetic as part of its long-term transformation strategy.
Instant is now the baseline for euro payments. Under the EU Instant Payments Regulation, payment service providers in the eurozone must receive instant credit transfers, send them at no higher price than a standard transfer, and offer a check of the payee’s name against the account before the payer authorizes a transfer. That turns SEPA Instant from a premium service into everyday volume that runs around the clock and settles in seconds, with fraud checks done inside the same window. ACI Connetic handles that load in one cloud-native architecture that combines payments processing, fraud prevention, payments intelligence and orchestration, so a bank can add capacity and new services without stitching separate systems together.
Solaris holds a full German banking license and runs accounts, cards, lending and payments for fintechs, digital brands and multinationals that build financial products into their own customer experiences. Those partners count on Solaris to move money on their behalf, which makes instant payments part of what they buy from it. Solaris selected ACI Connetic as the foundation of its payments modernization strategy. Together with majority shareholder SBI Group, it has also set out plans to develop its platform into pan-European financial infrastructure.
“Banks across Europe are rebuilding their payments around instant, and the ones moving fastest are making it a platform decision,” said Thomas Warsop, president and CEO of ACI Worldwide. “Solaris runs payments for an entire ecosystem of partners, so it needs infrastructure that grows with them. Bringing SEPA Instant onto ACI Connetic gives Solaris that foundation for its next phase of growth.”
“Going live on ACI Connetic is an important milestone in evolving our platform infrastructure,” said Steffen Jentsch, CEO of Solaris. “As Solaris matures into a Financial-Platform-as-a-Service provider, ACI Connetic gives us the scalable, robust foundation we need to deploy AI-driven, highly resilient payment processes that meet the highest European regulatory standards our partners and their customers expect.”

title: Crypto casino Duelbits goes offline after $7 million hot wallet hack
summary: Attackers drained Duelbits' hot wallets across four blockchains; about $6 million in stolen funds now sits in a single Ethereum address.
content: Crypto casino Duelbits has gone offline following a major hot wallet hack resulting in the theft of approximately $7 million. Attackers managed to drain funds across four different blockchains. Currently, about $6 million of the stolen assets have been traced and are being held in a single Ethereum address as investigations into the security breach continue.
content_ta: Crypto casino ஆன Duelbits-ல் நடந்த பெரிய hot wallet hack காரணமாக சுமார் $7 மில்லியன் திருடப்பட்டு, தற்காலிகமாக அது offline-க்குச் சென்றுள்ளது. நான்கு blockchains-ல் இருந்த funds-களை attackers திருடியுள்ளனர். இதில் சுமார் $6 மில்லியன் அளவிலான stolen funds தற்போது ஒரே ஒரு Ethereum address-ல் வைக்கப்பட்டுள்ளது.

title: European stablecoin issuer Qivalis sees transformation of global trade finance

content: European stablecoin issuer Qivalis believes the global trade finance sector is undergoing a major transformation. According to Jan-Oliver Sell, CEO and founder of Qivalis, the entire trade finance supply chain is transitioning toward the use of stablecoins, signaling a shift in how international transactions and financial processes are conducted across markets.

title: Crypto treasury model loses its edge as stock premiums fade: DWF
summary: Most DATs now trade below the value of their crypto holdings, weakening a financing model that once helped companies expand their balance sheets.
content: The crypto treasury model used by digital asset treasuries is losing its advantage as stock premiums fade. According to DWF, most DATs now trade below the actual value of their crypto holdings. This trend weakens a once-popular financing model that companies used to expand their balance sheets during favorable market conditions.
content_ta: டிஜிட்டல் அசெட் ட்ரெஷரிகளால் பயன்படுத்தப்படும் கிரிப்டோ ட்ரெஷரி மாதிரி, ஸ்டாக் பிரீமியம்கள் குறைந்து வருவதால் தனது நன்மையை இழந்து வருகிறது. DWF-இன் கூற்றுப்படி, பெரும்பாலான DATகள் இப்போது அவற்றின் கிரிப்டோ ஹோல்டிங்ஸின் உண்மையான மதித்திற்குக் கீழே வர்த்தகம் செய்யப்படுகின்றன. இந்தப் போக்கு, சாதகமான சந்தைச் சூழ்நிலையில் நிறுவனங்கள் தங்கள் இருப்புநிலைக் குறிப்புகளை விரிவுபடுத்த உதவிய ஒரு பிரபலமான நிதி மாதிரியை பலவீனப்படுத்துகிறது.

title: Sequans exits Bitcoin treasury strategy after selling remaining 314 BTC
summary: The France-based semiconductor company has fully unwound a Bitcoin treasury that once held more than 3,200 BTC as more firms scale back crypto holdings.
content: France-based semiconductor company Sequans has fully exited its Bitcoin treasury strategy. The firm sold its remaining 314 BTC, completely unwinding a crypto reserve that previously held over 3,200 BTC. This move highlights a broader trend of companies scaling back their corporate cryptocurrency holdings.
content_ta: பிரான்ஸ் நாட்டைச் சேர்ந்த செமிகண்டக்டர் நிறுவனமான Sequans, தனது Bitcoin கருவூல உத்தியிலிருந்து முழுமையாக வெளியேறியுள்ளது. இந்நிறுவனம் தனது வசம் இருந்த மீதமுள்ள 314 BTC-ஐ விற்றுள்ளது. இதன் மூலம், முன்பு 3,200-க்கும் மேற்பட்ட BTC-களை வைத்திருந்த தனது கிரிப்டோ கையிருப்புகளை இந்நிறுவனம் முழுமையாக விலக்கிக் கொண்டுள்ளது.

title: Solana Foundation hires ex-Binance CMO and payments exec as new partnerships expand

content: The Solana Foundation has strengthened its leadership team by hiring former Binance CMO Rachel Conlan and payments executive Jamal Raees. These strategic appointments come as the Solana Foundation expands its network with a wave of new partnerships.

title: £10K Reward Offered After UK Couple Attacked in Crypto Home Invasion

content: A £10,000 reward has been offered following a violent home invasion in the UK targeting a couple for cryptocurrency. Police believe the robbery was carefully planned and targeted. Investigators stated that instructions were relayed in real-time to the three attackers by a fourth man participating via a video call. Authorities are urging anyone with information to come forward as the investigation continues.

title: OpenZeppelin Integrates with TRON to Bring Its Security Standard to the Network
summary: LONDON, UK, September 24, 2026 – OpenZeppelin, the security standard for onchain finance and secure smart contract development, today announced that its smart contract libraries and secure development suite are now available for the TRON network.   The integration gives developers building on TRON access to OpenZeppelin’s widely used security-focused development framework, adapted specifically for the TRON network. Teams can now build applications using audited contract components, familiar upgrade workflows, and developer tooling designed around TRON’s standards and network capabilities.   OpenZeppelin’s TRON offering includes audited smart contract libraries, secure upgrade tools, and the Contracts Wizard, giving developers trusted building blocks for tokens, access control, governance, and applications that need to evolve over time. Built-in security checks and AI-assisted development support help teams build, deploy, and update applications with greater confidence.   “Security is fundamental to expanding what developers can build across the TRON ecosystem,” said Sam Elfarra, Community Spokesperson of the TRON DAO. “OpenZeppelin gives developers a trusted set of tools and standards that many already know from across the broader blockchain industry. Bringing that experience to TRON lowers friction for builders while giving teams stronger foundations for creating applications that can operate at scale.”   Designed around TRON’s specific network capabilities, the tools also support more advanced use cases, including passkey authentication, supply controls, permissions and governance. Together, they give developers a secure foundation for building applications while maintaining flexibility as the TRON network continues to evolve.   “Strong security starts at the foundation. Developers need primitives they can trust on the network they are deploying to,” said Pepe Blasco, Engineering Manager at OpenZeppelin. “Bringing our contracts and tooling to TRON lets teams keep the assurances they know from other ecosystems, while accounting for the network-specific requirements that matter in production. The goal is a robust path from first line to production.”   As TRON continues to support a growing range of applications across stablecoins, decentralized finance, payments and other on-chain use cases, the integration expands the tools available to developers and provides a strong foundation for building and scaling applications on the network.   About OpenZeppelin OpenZeppelin is the security standard for onchain finance. Since 2015, the company has set the bar for blockchain and smart contract security through the industry-standard OpenZeppelin Contracts library, behind $37 trillion in value transferred, and 900+ security engagements that have surfaced 10,000+ vulnerabilities before production. OpenZeppelin secures the world’s leading blockchain networks, DeFi protocols, institutions, and enterprises globally. Learn more at www.openzeppelin.com. title: mika Raises €6 Million to Make the Tax Adviser Optional for Germany’s Small Businesses
summary:
Berlin-based vertical AI startup mika has raised €6 million. Rather than digitalising the traditional tax firm, mika rebuilds accounting, tax and finance from the ground up as an AI-native financial operating system for SMEs. For small limited companies (GmbHs and UGs), mika manages ongoing bookkeeping, VAT returns, annual accounts and tax filings. The seed round is led by pan-European investor Smedvig Ventures. Also participating are Basel-based family office Wecken & Cie. (Care4 AG) alongside Dennis Bemmann and Michael Brehm (co-founders of studiVZ), Johannes Ditterich (limango founder) and Martina Pfeifer (encourageventures). Additionally, existing investors Keen Venture Partners and Dutch Founders Fund increased their stakes. The fresh capital will fund growth and the further development of the platform.
 
Founders should be building their business, not sorting through receipts
 
Germany has almost a million small incorporated businesses, most of them GmbHs (private limited companies) and their smaller cousin, the UG. Bookkeeping, VAT returns and annual accounts are a legal requirement for every one of them. In theory, a company's management can do all of this itself. In practice, almost no one does. One wrong entry can trigger back-taxes or penalties, and the rules are scattered across tax codes that change on a yearly basis. Instead, almost every small company hands its bookkeeping and filings over to a tax adviser or firm.
 
Agnieszka Walorska knows the problem well. She grew up without entrepreneurial role models and had no family money or network behind her when she started her first company. A few thousand euros a year for a tax adviser may be a rounding error for some, but for others, it is the reason a company never gets founded. For anyone without savings or the right connections, this is how German bureaucracy becomes a barrier to entry.
 

"The moment you start a GmbH in Germany, you're told you need a tax adviser. It goes so far that some founders think it's a legal requirement. To me, it's obvious that this cannot be how it works,” says Agnieszka Walorska, Founder and CEO of mika. "At mika, we use AI to tear down that barrier, so that your bank balance or the family you were born into no longer decides who gets to start a company.”
 
Agnieszka Walorska leads mika together with Luke Linnekuhle (CFO) and Henry Müssemann (CTO). Linnekuhle helped build the finance function at activewear brand Oceansapart. Müssemann was previously Head of Engineering at Freezingdata, a digital-forensics software provider he helped build to its exit.
“Nowhere else in Europe is accounting and tax as demanding or costly for small businesses as in Germany, where the two are so tightly linked that a single mistake carries straight through to the tax bill. It is the reason big international players never gained a foothold here, and why SMEs were left with no real alternative,” says Freddie Kalfayan, Principal at Smedvig Ventures. “mika is the first to build for this reality instead of around it, and its customers demonstrate some of the strongest enthusiasm we have seen across our portfolio.”
AI and accountants working the same books
 
Behind mika is its own AI-native general ledger, purpose-made for German accounting. The AI reads and understands every receipt and every payment. Depending on the task, different AI models come into play, embedded in the domain knowledge and rules mika has developed itself.
 
mika's AI categorises every transaction, records it correctly and explains to users what each entry means, usually without anyone lifting a finger. Trained accountants in-house check the results and step in wherever the complexity calls for a human. There is also something a tax firm cannot offer. You can talk to your own numbers, either inside mika or through a standard AI interface, the Model Context Protocol (MCP), in assistants such as ChatGPT or Claude.
 
mika takes care of the small stuff too. Upload a baffling letter from the tax office and it's explained on the spot, along with what to do next. Questions about your own accounts and finances are answered by the AI chat straight away, even on a Sunday evening. Individual tax advice is not yet part of the offering. For that, mika works with licensed tax advisers from its network.
 
Revenue growing more than 20 per cent every month
At the start of the year, around 400 GmbHs and UGs used mika. Today there are more than 750. mika began with digital-first service businesses such as agencies and consultancies. Its customers now also come from Software-as-a-Service (SaaS), property and e-commerce, with retail and the skilled trades the most recent to join. The company's revenue has climbed by more than 20 per cent every month, and in July 2026 it passed €1 million in annual revenue.
„With mika we haven't simply brought in a new piece of software, we've added a digital team member to our accounting. It's fascinating to watch AI free us up to focus on strategy, creativity and our customers. For us it's proof that AI can genuinely take work off people's hands rather than replace them,“ says Kolja Sagorski, founder of patchletter.
"When we invested in 2024, the 'AI plus human' model was seen as a niche. For many it was too much service and too little software,” says Djoni de Vos, Principal at Keen Venture Partners. "Today, many investors describe that exact model as the next big category, service as software. mika proved its viability before it had a name.”

The company provides an AI-native financial operating system designed for small businesses in Germany to manage bookkeeping, VAT returns, and tax filings, aiming to reduce the reliance on traditional tax advisers.

title: Crux Analytics Raises $2.2M Seed Round to Help Financial Institutions Win More Small Business Clients Without Adding Headcount
summary:
Crux Analytics, the fintech fixing the relationship between financial services companies and the small businesses they serve, has raised $2.2 million in seed funding to help institutions engage, acquire and retain high-potential business relationships, bringing its total funding to $3.2 million.
Crux’s seed round is backed by the very institutions it was built to serve. Castle Creek Launchpad, a joint venture fund with 34 community banks as limited partners, led the raise, with additional participation from Chartway Ventures, One Washington Financial and Curql, three leading credit union investment funds. This funding will enable Crux Analytics to expand its team and accelerate product development as the company capitalises on strong market momentum and a growing portfolio and pipeline of financial services providers, which started with community banks and credit unions and has now expanded organically.
Crux Analytics was founded in 2023 by brothers Jacob and Nathan Bennett, driven by Jacob's firsthand experience of the challenges small businesses face when seeking banking support. As a former small business owner and consultant to Fortune 500 companies, Jacob witnessed how traditional financial institutions consistently underserved small businesses in comparison to their larger counterparts.
Addressing the Challenge of Supporting Small Businesses
Small businesses drive nearly half of all private-sector employment and more than 44% of the U.S.' GDP, yet the key partners supporting them face a fundamental scaling challenge. Serving small businesses is relationship-driven, which requires significant human capital and resources. Large banks can simply hire more people to manage those relationships, but smaller financial services companies need a smarter approach: technology that multiplies their employees' productivity and lets them deliver the trusted-advisor relationship their clients want without exponentially growing their team.
Institutional employees currently spend the majority of their time on the operational tasks required to build a client deal, not on core relationship building with the business owner. Crux replaces the traditional sales enablement stack with a sales execution engine, allowing employees to spend more time closing deals and serving as a trusted advisor.
Community financial institutions remain in robust financial health, operating in a markedly friendlier regulatory environment than they have in years. Community banks closed out 2025 with full-year net income of $29.9B, a 22.5% increase over 2024, with net interest margin reaching 3.77% in the fourth quarter, the highest level since 2018. That strength has carried into 2026: community bank pretax return on assets stood at 1.42% in the first quarter, up 26 basis points year-over-year, and net interest margin remains 24 basis points above its year-ago level.
Credit unions are in equally strong shape: the sector's net worth ratio reached 11.24% in the first quarter of 2026, up from 10.95% a year earlier and more than 60% above the 7% regulatory threshold for a well-capitalized institution, with net income totaling $20.4B at an annual rate, up 30.5% from the same period in 2025.
The platform delivers agentic business development workflows, helping users identify, research and prioritize high-potential prospects, execute targeted personalized outreach, and actively monitor relationships as they evolve. The result is a streamlined workflow that drives new revenue and asset growth, and improves efficiency. Institutions win more small business clients, deepen existing relationships, and build a stickier, more durable client base in the process.
Jacob Bennett, CEO and Co-founder of Crux Analytics, comments: “This funding comes at a critical time. We built Crux for community banks and credit unions, and what we learned there is that the same relationship problem exists across the small business economy. Alternative lenders, commercial insurers and real estate operators all win on relationships, and they all lose time to the operational work that sits behind them. We're giving those teams the infrastructure to act on what they know about their clients, so growth comes from deeper relationships rather than bigger headcount."
Jurgen van de Vyver from Castle Creek Launchpad, said: "Having worked closely with community banks through our strategic limited partners, we've seen how these institutions are built for relationships but lack the operational tools to deliver on that promise at scale. Driving outbound sales has always been a challenge for community banks, which historically have relied on referrals from their local networks. More banks are now looking for new ways to chase organic growth, and their business relationships are crucial to achieving that. Crux Analytics unlocks that potential by automating the manual work so community banks can focus on what matters most, building meaningful relationships with local business owners."
Rob Keatts from Chartway Ventures, added: "The credit union industry has always been built on community relationships, but scaling that approach to serve local businesses has proven difficult. Crux Analytics removes the operational barriers, empowering credit unions to become the community business banking partners they ought to be. When credit unions can proactively support their business members, entire communities benefit from stronger local economies."
NoYesFundraising News24 Sep, 2026
content: Crux Analytics has raised $2.2 million in a seed funding round led by Castle Creek Launchpad, bringing its total funding to $3.2 million. The fintech platform helps financial institutions such as community banks and credit unions efficiently acquire and retain small business clients without expanding their headcount. The new capital will be used to expand the team and accelerate product development.
content_ta: Crux Analytics நிறுவனம் Castle Creek Launchpad தலைமையில் நடைபெற்ற முதலீட்டு சுற்றில் 2.2 மில்லியன் டாலர்களை திரட்டியுள்ளது. இதன் மூலம் நிறுவனத்தின் மொத்த நிதி திரட்டல் 3.2 மில்லியன் டாலராக உயர்ந்துள்ளது. கம்யூனிட்டி வங்கிகள் மற்றும் கிரெடிட் யூனியன்கள் போன்ற நிதி நிறுவனங்கள் தங்கள் பணியாளர்களின் எண்ணிக்கையை அதிகரிக்காமலேயே சிறு வணிக வாடிக்கையாளர்களை ஈர்க்கவும் தக்கவைக்கவும் இந்த ஃபின்டெக் தளம் உதவுகிறது.
